stories.title: AI agents move from chatbots toward autonomous workflows
stories.subtitle: Companies are increasingly experimenting with systems that can plan and execute multi-step tasks.
stories.summary: The latest wave of AI products is moving beyond simple question-and-answer interfaces toward agents capable of completing longer workflows. The shift is creating opportunities for businesses to automate research, customer support, operations and software development.
stories.shortSummary: AI is increasingly shifting from answering questions to completing multi-step tasks.

keyPoints: AI products are increasingly designed around task completion.
Agent systems can combine multiple tools and models.
Businesses are testing agents for repetitive workflows.
Reliability remains a major challenge.

explain.title: Why this matters
explain.answer: The important shift is from AI as an interface to AI as a worker that can complete a sequence of tasks. This could change how software products are designed and create new opportunities for startups building specialized agents.
evidence: Multiple sources describe increased interest in multi-step AI workflows.
The trend is appearing across software and business automation products.

explain.title: Why this matters
explain.answer: Infrastructure businesses can benefit from the growing amount of compute and software required by AI applications, although they can also face high capital requirements.

explain.title: Why this matters
explain.answer: For AI businesses, infrastructure efficiency directly affects operating costs. Improvements in performance per watt could make some AI workloads cheaper to run.

messages.content: Good morning. Here are today's most relevant stories across AI, startups, technology and business.
What is the biggest AI trend today?
The strongest theme is the shift toward AI agents and multi-step workflows. Several sources describe AI systems moving from answering questions toward completing tasks.
